text:
[RARC.5.6.9] The loop is **strictly serial** within an engine. Parallelism
across tiers comes from running engines on separate threads or in separate
processes, which is the integrator's choice. Within one engine there is no
parallelism at the event level: `seq` is assigned as each event is produced
and increases monotonically ([LFST.5.3]).

idris.name: rarc_5_6_9__assign
idris.note: Step (1): pull the next event and stamp it. Models the serial shape -- one counter, advancing once per event -- but ASSUMES seriality rather than establishing it. That the loop is strictly serial is a design constraint on an implementation, not a proposition a model of the loop can prove about itself.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_9__count_from
idris.note: What a monotonic counter produces: start, start+1, start+2, one per event. Defined independently of `assign` so the positionality theorem has something to be a theorem ABOUT -- derived from `assign` it would restate it rather than check it.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_9__seq_is_positional
idris.note: MONOTONICITY IN THE FORM A REPLAYER CAN USE. The seq values a pass assigns depend only on the starting counter and the NUMBER of events, never on the events themselves -- so two runs seeing the same number of events agree on every seq before either looks at a payload. Strictly stronger than `increasing`, which would admit seq = hash(payload) sorted ascending: monotonic and useless. Does NOT establish that the loop's OUTPUT is deterministic -- positional seq orders the events identically and says nothing about what processing each produces, which is the half [RARC.5.6.10] needs and the corpus does not supply.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_9__seqs
idris.note: The seq values a pass assigned, in order.
